title: hso-dataverse-architect spec.json (v2)
description: The machine-readable design sidecar the architect emits alongside the markdown spec. SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH: the architect validates against it (Validate-SpecJson), the executor renders from it (BuildAllForms / CurateDefaultViews), and every grader (Grade-Metadata, Grade-SliceFidelity, Grade-SolutionExport, Assert-SpecFormsBuilt) diffs the build against it. A Main form's `tabs` here IS the BuildForm LayoutSpec verbatim, so the spec fully specifies — and is reviewable as — the form that gets built.

fieldRef.description: A column on the form, by logical name (string) or as an object for extra placement hints.

subgrid.description: A subgrid cell surfacing a child table on the form (Build-SubgridCellXml). Bind a DEDICATED, parent-excluding view, not the default public view.

target.description: Child table logical name the grid lists.

relationship.description: 1:N relationship schema name binding the grid.

view.description: Saved view (name or id) the grid binds.

section.description: A form section. Normally carries at least one of fields / subgrid / timeline.

timeline.description: Render the timeline control here (table must have Notes or Activities enabled).

lane.description: A vertical lane (form <column>). Lane widths across a tab MUST sum to 100.

width.description: Lane width, e.g. '60%' or '60'. Widths in a tab sum to 100.

header.description: The KPI header (at-a-glance metrics). Max 4 fields. Mandatory for Patterns A/B/C.

catalogRelease.description: BPC catalog release the brief mapped against (e.g. "JUL 2026") — copied verbatim from the brief's catalogRelease frontmatter, never re-derived (ADR 0047 / ADR 0048 A1). Omit when the brief carries no process mapping.

frProcessMap.description: BPC process tags propagated verbatim from the Requirements Brief's Process Mapping section (ADR 0047) — one entry per FR the spec implements. Per-slice work items derive their BPC tags from this map via the slice's fr_refs. Optional — omit when the brief carries no process mapping.

processSequenceId.description: BPC ProcessSequenceId, verbatim from the catalog release — fully-qualified padded form, e.g. "65.20.025.000" (JUL 2026+). Treat as an opaque string; never trim .000 padding. Omit for proposed-custom/unmapped.

levelPath.description: Human-readable lineage, e.g. "85 Prospect to quote › 85.40 Manage sales orders".

proposalKey.description: The brief's custom-process proposal key when status is proposed-custom.

solution.description: The solution UNIQUE NAME the executor creates/uses — the grader discovers the build by this name.

columns.description: The declared data model: every custom column the spec proposes, one entry per (table, name). The validator cross-checks every forms[].header/section field and views[].column against this set (plus system columns and the table's primary name column) — an invented or suffixed field reference fails the spec. Required whenever forms or views are declared.

name.description: Column logical name, exactly as declared in the markdown data model (hso_<fieldname>_<suffix> pattern).

newTables.description: Net-new custom tables this spec introduces (logical names). Required (possibly empty) whenever the spec declares publisher-owned tables. A non-empty list requires the dedicated semantic-research.md skill-run artifact (hso-semantic-data-modeling) in the spec folder, mentioning every listed table — the semantic-research gate keys on this declaration.

forms.description: One entry per form. For a Main form, `tabs` is the full BuildForm LayoutSpec and is REQUIRED — the spec specifies the whole form (tabs, lanes, sections, fields, KPI header) so it can be reviewed and rendered deterministically. The executor synthesizes a layout only as a fallback for specs that omit it.

timeline.description: The recorded per-form timeline verdict — ground truth for whether a missing timeline is a defect or an intentional design choice. Must agree with any section that sets timeline:true.

layoutPattern.description: Layout pattern. A/B/C are two-lane KPI-header forms; D (hub) and E (simple) are single-lane. Drives the header and lane-count expectations the grader enforces.

recordLog.description: Set false to opt out of the auto-appended HSO Record Log tab (SOP §6). Defaults to appended.

formDescription.description: Layout rationale recorded in the form Description (spec traceability).

tabs.description: Full form layout = the BuildForm LayoutSpec. Required for Main forms.

views.description: Public views per table. Declare `columns` (the visible column set, in order) so the grader diffs the built view against the spec instead of only counting to a floor.

type.description: View type. A lookup view must be 'Lookup' (the executor updates the table's existing querytype=64 lookup view, not a new Public view); default is PublicView.

columns.description: Visible columns by logical name, in display order — the grader diffs the built view's layoutxml cells against this set.

isDefault.description: Whether this is the table's default public view (e.g. the shipped 'Active <x>').

activeFilter.description: True when the view must filter statecode=0 (any 'Active *' view).

lookupOnChild.description: Lookup logical name on the CHILD (side-count rule).

ownedBySlice.description: Slice id that builds the lookup.

mappings.description: Optional attribute mappings (opt-in; no defaults). Fields auto-populated on the CHILD when it is created from the PARENT's subgrid (+New) — fires only on create-from-parent, not on import or direct create. The parent lookup is always set automatically and need not be listed.

source.description: PARENT column logical name to copy from.

target.description: CHILD column logical name to copy to (must be type-compatible with source).

mode.description: HITL is legal ONLY on a `design` slice (an architect-owned decision node), and every design slice is HITL — build slices are AFK by definition. Design nodes are settled at spec approval (the grill gate): a SIGNED spec carries zero HITL slices, because approval IS the authorization for every slice. Validate-SpecJson enforces HITL⇔design always, and -Signed refuses any remaining HITL/design slice (E2E round-3, the HITL/OQ episode).

preconditions.description: Environment preconditions this slice's build/acceptance needs that Dataverse metadata alone does not provide — a Power Pages site, a deployed plugin package, a connection reference, an environment variable value. The delivery pipeline probes every declared precondition at Stage 0 (preflight) and halts with a clear ask BEFORE any slice builds; a slice that would otherwise discover the gap mid-Stage-1 (round-3 s14: no Power Pages site in the target env) declares it here. Validate-SpecJson REQUIRES a `power-pages-site` precondition on any slice whose touches name a portal / Power Pages surface.

kind.description: What must exist. power-pages-site = a provisioned Power Pages site in the target env (probe: powerpagesites / adx_websites); plugin-package = a deployed pluginpackage; connection-reference / environment-variable = the named record with a value; app-module = an existing app (extend targets); other = free-form, `probe` mandatory.

detail.description: What exactly must exist (site name / package name / reference logical name / variable schema name).

probe.description: How Stage 0 checks it (an entity-set query or command). Required when kind is `other`; defaults per kind otherwise.

askIfMissing.description: The human action the pipeline reports when the probe fails (e.g. 'provision the Power Pages site <name> in <env> before dispatch').

budgetAccepted.description: Records the architect's decision to keep a slice whole after Validate-SpecJson flagged it over the rule-9 context budget (structural caps: one heavy concern per slice; estimate is a tripwire, not truth). The value is the REASON the slice must not be split (e.g. 'single plugin assembly - cannot split further; nothing else rides in it'). Like an Open-Question disposition: silence is not a valid state - a flagged slice without this field fails the -Signed Stage-0 gate. Omit on unflagged slices; a stale entry on an unflagged slice draws an advisory.

fr_refs.description: Functional-requirement ids from the brief this slice implements (e.g. "FR-1"). Resolved to work items through the brief's ADO Tracking map; the delivery pipeline's attribution claims are built from this chain. Optional — omit when the engagement has no FR/ADO tracking.

acceptance.description: Env-validated acceptance for THIS slice — the per-slice review gate checks the built slice against it.

adoProjection.description: ADO Build Management projection (ADR 0048) — derived at spec-authoring time so the grill gate reviews it with the DAG. 1:1 slice→work-item, never split a slice to fit the type taxonomy. Omit when the engagement does not track build work items.

buildType.description: Deterministic precedence over the slice's touches: Data Migration › Integration › Workflow (cloud flow) › Report (incl. dashboards) › Security role › Extension default (Extension covers maker-portal configuration as well as code). Always "none" for design slices.

relatedTargets.description: Optional-Related link targets per build-type lineage (template-owner ruling 2026-07-22): FR ids (resolved to Requirement work items via the brief's ADO Tracking map) for Extension-class items; BPC process/process-area ProcessSequenceIds for Data Migration-class items.

workItemId.description: The created Build Management work item id — assigned by the pipeline's grill-approval batch-create (ADR 0048 choreography), not by the architect.

choices.description: Global option sets as a declared contract: the executor renders the exact options (label, value, optional color) and the grader diffs the built set against this. Omit `value` to auto-generate it.

value.description: Explicit option value; omit to auto-generate in the publisher range.

statusReasons.description: Declared statuscode lifecycle per table: the full set of status reasons mapped to state (0=Active, 1=Inactive) with the default-active value flagged. The executor renders the whole lifecycle (every value + the default) and the grader diffs it — closing the weak-tier 'stops at the shipped 2-value default' gap.

value.description: Explicit statuscode value; omit to auto-generate.

default.description: Marks the single default-active statuscode (exactly one option should set this).

dashboards.description: Declared dashboards as a reachability contract. 'Built' is not 'reachable': a dashboard created, published, and registered as an app component is still invisible if no sitemap node points at it (the §1 gap that shipped three invisible dashboards). Every dashboard a persona is meant to see MUST declare how it is surfaced.

ownedBySlice.description: Slice id that builds the dashboard.

surfacedVia.description: How a persona reaches it: the id of a dashboard subarea in app.areas[].groups[].subAreas[] (one whose `dashboard` opens this), OR 'unsurfaced: <reason>' to deliberately record a non-navigable dashboard with its justification. A bare table name or empty string is not acceptable.

customApis.description: Declared Custom APIs whose INVOCATION SURFACE is part of the contract. The API's server behavior is designed in the markdown spec/SOP; this array exists so the design declares HOW a user invokes each user-facing API. A Custom API with a runtime invoker (or none) but no command surface is a server operation no user can reach — the §10 gap that shipped six user-facing operations with zero buttons and zero web resources. Per HSO ruling (2026-06-13), executeprivilegename is intentionally NOT modeled here (table privileges govern; absence is not a finding).

userInvocable.description: True when a human persona is meant to trigger this API directly (commit/correct an amendment, submit a memo, act on an approval step, preview/apply a reassignment). False for APIs invoked only by flows, admin scripts, or other code.

invoker.description: For a non-user-invocable API, the runtime caller (e.g. 'flow: hso_OnApproveStep', 'admin script', 'plugin') — records that the absent UI is intentional, not a gap.

commandSurface.description: REQUIRED when userInvocable is true: exactly how the persona invokes the API. Absence on a user-invocable API IS the §10 finding.

location.description: Where the command appears (modern command / appaction location 0/1/2). Authoring recipe: hso-dataverse-ui-config references/appaction-command-registration.md (SubGrid is flagged UNPROVEN there).

visibility.description: Visibility / enable rule — Power Fx binding or a precise description (e.g. 'enabled only when statuscode = Draft').

callingScript.description: Web resource + JS function that calls the API — the form-script half (hso-formscript-development). Naming the script forces it to actually be written, not just designed.

ownedBySlice.description: The UI-invocation slice that registers the command and deploys the web resource (the slice type the §10 lesson adds).

app.description: Model-driven app sitemap as a declared contract. The executor renders this (BuildSiteMap — one PATCH + publish + read-back) and the grader diffs the built sitemap against it. Areas -> Groups -> SubAreas, in declared order.

mode.description: create = build a NEW app from this definition (BuildSiteMap self-creates it; default). extend = add to an EXISTING app by its uniqueName (the app must already exist) — required for non-copyable OOB apps like the Customer Service workspace, which must be extended in place, not recreated. See the app-module SOP.

uniqueName.description: App module unique name. For mode=extend this MUST be the existing/OOB app's unique name (the extend target).

unsurfacedTables.description: Publisher-owned tables this spec declares (newTables[] / forms / views) that DELIBERATELY get no sitemap subarea, each with the reason (e.g. an intersect/detail table reached only through its parent's subgrid). Every other publisher-owned table MUST be a subAreas[].entity — Validate-SpecJson fails a spec table that is neither (E2E round-3 F-02: 13 reference tables built and never registered in the app). Unsurfaced means NO NAV NODE, not absent from the app: BuildSiteMap still registers every table listed here as an app component (a subgrid cannot open records of a table the app does not contain), and the reviewer's app-membership sweep covers it. The reason says how a persona reaches it.

items.description: A sitemap nav node. It opens EXACTLY ONE target: a table (entity), a dashboard, or a raw URL. A dashboard subarea is how a built dashboard becomes reachable — without one the dashboard is invisible no matter that it exists ('built' is not 'reachable').

entity.description: Table logical name this subarea opens.

dashboard.description: Dashboard (id or display name) this subarea opens. Classic dashboards render as a Url subarea bound to DefaultDashboard; the executor resolves the binding (hso-dataverse-ui-config Add-SiteMapSubArea -DefaultDashboard).

viewId.description: Optional default view (id or name) for the subarea.
